## Body

**Performance: PASS WITH NOTES** at `bac14b24689af8797e9a8fb8f75c8399228cad76`.

F144 part 2 over merged #192 (`9603be6`). The final merge changes no bytes from `d6163063`; the boot switch, shared cold-check helper and spawn-site guards are unchanged.

**Off remains no-I/O:** the first statement of `idle_nudge::round` checks `Services::idle_nudge` and returns an empty Vec. No qualification/schema read, map, status read, random mint, mark, message or FYI occurs. The existing shared watchdog still runs; only this component is constant-check/empty-return work.

**Enabled qualification is three global data queries plus one schema PRAGMA per round**, not three per seat:

| Query | Work visited and retained |
|---|---|
| `TASK_HOLDINGS_SQL` | Scans the `community_assignments_open_by_seat` partial index. `instance != ''` is a residual filter; nonempty instances are decoded and checked in process. Cost follows all open holding rows R and visited instance bytes, not only qualifying task holders. |
| `WORK_CLAIMS_SQL` | Scans `claims_open_by_seat`, filters `plan`/`fix`, returns distinct seats. Cost follows open claim rows C, not only the returned matching seats. |
| `UNANSWERED_REQUESTS_SQL` | Reads holder/project/role/instance from `role_requests`, filtering delivered, unanswered, nonnull holder. It does not materialize request bodies or read `closed_role_requests`. Cost follows rows still in the live table Q; it is not a keyed per-holder seek. |

**P195-N001:** answering stamps `answered_at`; it does not itself archive the row. Explicit close moves/deletes it transactionally. Therefore answered-but-not-closed rows can remain in Q even though they never qualify. This is an open-table scan bound, not a fixed unanswered-result bound or a scan of the closed history.

Qualification builds a BTreeSet of K seats and a BTreeMap of U returned request records: ordered inserts/comparisons plus their metadata bytes. If K=0, it returns before the snapshot map. Otherwise the existing reference map visits S snapshot rows once, followed by K lookups/filter tests; no S x K membership scan or individual nonholder query. With idle candidates, the existing global pending-compaction read follows.

Regular numeric task checks visit at most nine digits plus the optional letter. The `f<digits>` branch has no explicit length cap; legacy oversized F-like fields remain data-sized. New admission's name cap does not establish a cap on every restored field.

Per idle candidate, own-event/hour/mark checks retain their existing budget. Only due unmarked candidates reach the owner-job seek, queue peek and existing holdings/claims reads. `due()` filters those freshly read holdings/claims without adding a query. Requests are borrowed from the round's qualification snapshot, not re-read individually. Labels/project deduplication now include only qualified items; request metadata adds data-sized label and message work. Prior uncapped holding/request count and invalid-field scan qualifications remain.

**Cold check is moved, not duplicated:** old `wake_pa_receipt` called `audit_cold_wake`, which called `cold_wake::verdict` once. The new nudge calls that same verdict once and then calls `delivery.accept` directly only for Clear/Busy. It does not call the old forced-wake helper afterwards. The same session-status read, timeout and rare stale-working checks remain per winning due occurrence, not per global tick or per prime.

Cold, Unknown and check errors skip the seat's delivery and nudge-body construction, preserve the existing once-per-stretch mark/audit, and hold the cold FYI for each distinct live prime or fallback parent. The old forced-cold-wake audit/send is removed from this path. Cold attempts still pay the mark, owner-ID mint, status check, prime lookup, independent FYI mints/storage and final audit; they are not resource-free. Warm attempts retain the ordinary send and FYIs.

No new loop, timer, poll, executable site, migration or community writer commit. Fewer seats can reach the per-seat paths; a bare specialist alone no longer qualifies. The switch remains default off until intentionally enabled at daemon start.
